depth._note: best_m set from 6 logged dives at 4-10 m - that is where you actually hunt, not the 8-18 m I guessed.

shelter._note: swell_weight splits shelter between wind fetch and swell fetch. Wind alone missed old swell running in from a different quarter than today's breeze.

visibility._note: Checked against 6 logged dives Aug 2026: predicted 12-13 m while actual ran 5-10 m, correlation r=+0.07. This model is NOT yet predictive. viz_max lowered and the wave term demoted; the real fix is calibrate.py --fit-viz once ~15 dives are logged.

thermocline._note: How much colder it is at depth than at the surface, by month (Jan..Dec). The north Adriatic stratifies hard in summer, so surface temperature says nothing about where a demersal fish actually sits. These are estimates - check them against your dive computer and edit.

light._note: Sun elevation shapes the hourly score. 0 below the horizon (night spearfishing is prohibited in Croatia); best at low sun; worst under flat high sun.

wind_regimes._note: Direction the wind blows FROM, degrees. First match wins.

bora.note: Offshore, cold and gusty. Short fetch at the coast so the water often runs clear, but the surface is hard work and gusts build fast.

jugo.note: Onshore and warm, pushes long swell and turbid water in. The classic viz-killer here; it can take days to clear after.

maestral.note: Summer afternoon thermal. Builds from midday and dies at dusk, so morning and evening stay workable.

tramontana.note: Cold northerly off the land. Generally clean water, choppy surface.

cmems._note: Real temperature at depth, replacing the thermocline guesses. Credentials come from the COPERNICUSMARINE_SERVICE_USERNAME and COPERNICUSMARINE_SERVICE_PASSWORD environment variables, set as GitHub Actions secrets. NEVER put a username or password in this file - it is committed to a public repository. Falls back to the thermocline estimate automatically if credentials are missing or the service is unreachable.

water._note: min_width_cells severs narrow channels; require_sea_connection then discards whatever is left inland. EMODnet carries the Mirna estuary several km up the valley and it was being scored as diveable sea.

overlay._note: Defaults reproduce the original appearance. Knobs if you want to change it: supersample 2 halves the block size at 4x the file size; raising alpha_floor_score hides low-scoring water so only candidate spots are painted.

contours._note: Depth lines drawn on the map. Orientation only, not navigation.

bathymetry._note: auto picks EMODnet (~115 m) inside European seas and GMRT elsewhere. GMRT merges research multibeam over a global base, so the resolution varies by how well surveyed a coast is - the code measures what arrives rather than trusting this file. Falls back down the chain GMRT -> SRTM15+ if a source is down, so an outage costs quality, not the region.

wrecks._note: Charted wrecks from OpenStreetMap. Point data, so unaffected by bathymetry resolution - the one structure signal that is as good in Bali as in Istria.
